finding: This is an outcome recorded after the period, and it encodes claims. It is present for 2023 and 2024 but absent in 2025, so it is leakage and also unavailable for the test year.
evidence: Missing share: fit2023 0.000, A2024 0.000, test2025 1.000. PSI fit2023->test2025 is about 18.1-18.2. Rows with 'declined_by_insurer' that have a claim: developed 0.970 / 0.991 / 0.947 and fit2023 1.000 / 1.000 / 0.981 (buildings / contents / motor), against 0.03-0.14 for 'renewed'.
recommendation: Exclude it from every model and every derived feature. No model uses it today; this is a guard.

finding: The count is driven by claims, which confirms D-04. Test rows show the level of customers who have not claimed, so its 2025 distribution differs structurally from training.
evidence: Mean contacts, claimants against non-claimants: developed 3.05 / 3.05 / 3.28 against 0.42 / 0.41 / 0.41. Correlation with n_claims: 0.57 / 0.56 / 0.75 developed, 0.60 / 0.52 / 0.78 fit2023. Mean in test2025 is 0.398 / 0.399 / 0.400, against fit2023 0.558 / 0.513 / 0.857 and fit2023 non-claimants 0.452 / 0.436 / 0.438. Motor PSI fit2023->test2025 is 0.273.
recommendation: Never use it, including as a band (f_cs_contacts) or inside any interaction.

line: buildings (C0 XGB input); also motor and contents raw
finding: It is an exact duplicate of tenure plus a calendar drift, and it is the one C0 input that newly leaves the developed training range in 2025. customer_since_year equal to the row's year is the same thing as new business, and 2025 rows reach the value 2025, which the developed market never had. The 2025 renewals who joined in 2024 sit on a value that in developed 2024 meant new business only.
evidence: On 100% of rows in every split: yr - customer_since_year = renewal_count, and customer_since_year = yr if and only if new_business. Share of test2025 exposure above the developed maximum (2024): 0.768, and above the fit2023 maximum: 0.81. For fit2023 and A2024 the share above the developed maximum is 0. PSI fit2023->test2025 is 8.53. 4.2% of 2025 exposure is renewals with customer_since_year = 2024; developed rows with customer_since_year = 2024 are 100% new business.
recommendation: Replace it with tenure = yr - customer_since_year, which equals renewal_count, or drop it, because renewal_count already carries the information. For buildings, test a C0 variation without the raw year, tuned by grouped CV within 2023.

finding: This is a data-window artefact, not a risk factor. A code is present exactly when the customer joined inside the observed window: from 2021 in the developed data and from 2023 in the emerging data. In fit2023 it duplicates new_business perfectly. In 2025 it also tags the renewals who joined in 2023-24, so a relativity learnt in 2023 would wrongly treat those renewals as new business.
evidence: P(code present | new business) is 1.000 in every split. P(code present | renewal): fit2023 0.000, A2024 0.12, test2025 0.27-0.28, developed 0.20. Code present by customer_since_year: 2020 0.00, 2021-24 1.00 (developed); 2022 0.00, 2023-25 1.00 (emerging). Missing share: fit2023 0.88, test2025 0.17. PSI fit2023->test2025 is 2.51-2.55. PSI renewals 2023 -> new business 2023 is 15.7.
recommendation: Drop it from the technical model and from buildings C0 variations. If a 'joined since 2023' flag is wanted, derive it from tenure.

finding: The new-business flag changes meaning in 2025. In training it marks customers who joined mid-year with partial-year exposure. In 2025 it marks a block that incepts in early January for close to a full year. Covariate profiles of new business barely change from 2023 to 2025, so the younger 2025 book is a mix effect. In motor, C0 under-predicts 2023 new business by about 1.9 times, and the gap holds for January-quarter joiners too.
evidence: Share of new-business rows incepting in January: fit2023 0.07, test2025 0.88-0.91. Median inception day: 189-196 against 9. Mean new-business exposure: 0.46-0.48 against 0.88-0.92. Share of exposure that is new business: fit2023 0.062-0.064, test2025 0.768-0.770. PSI from 2023 new business to 2025 new business is at most 0.06 on every non-weather field (age band 0.002-0.005). Share aged 17-24 in test2025: new business 0.275, renewals 0.157-0.161. Relative A/E of C0, new business against renewals, fit2023, with a customer bootstrap: motor 1.94 [1.24, 2.90] on 265 claim rows; buildings 0.89 [0.35, 1.65]; contents 1.01 [0.51, 1.62]. Motor first-quarter new business: 1.55 on 102 claim rows, with frequency ratio only 1.04, so the gap is mainly severity. In the developed market, January new business has relative A/E 1.08 / 1.16 / 1.04 against mid-year 1.06 / 0.98 / 1.03.
recommendation: Keep a single new-business or tenure encoding. Do not apply a new-business relativity estimated on 2023 mid-year joiners at full credibility to the 2025 January block. Motor is the only line with a statistically significant new-business signal (2023 only; C2a was rejected on 2023->2024).

finding: This is a commercial pricing output that partly encodes new business. The 10% discount is given only to new business, and in a very different proportion in each market, so the same level means different things across markets. Within the emerging data it is stable from 2023 to 2025.
evidence: Share of renewals with a 10% discount: 0.000 in every market and year. Share of new business with a 10% discount: developed 0.349, emerging 0.045-0.057 (test2025 0.050). PSI from 2023 to 2025 new business: 0.000-0.001. PSI fit2023->test2025: 0.059-0.062, from mix only. PSI developed->fit2023: 0.23.
recommendation: Treat it like written_premium: an owner decision alongside D-05, or drop it. Never carry the developed relativity for the 10% level into the emerging market.

finding: About 23% of emerging exposure lies above the developed maximum, but that is equally true in 2023 and 2024, so it is not a 2025 shift. It is almost all in regions E02 and E04, where wildfire and region are confounded. C0's trees stay flat beyond the developed range. The 2023 evidence that C0 under-prices these rows is not significant and comes from severity.
evidence: Developed maximum is 0.615. Share of exposure above it: fit2023 0.252, A2024 0.228, test2025 0.230. In fit2023, share above it by region: E02 0.99, E04 1.00, E01 0.13, E06 0.07, E03 and E05 0. Relative A/E of C0, rows above against below, fit2023: 1.69 [95% 0.80, 2.94] on 122 claim rows; claim frequency per unit of C0 0.92; with row cost capped at 50k, 1.34. In the developed market, C0's in-sample A/E by wildfire decile is 0.92-1.09, and raw loss cost rises only from 401 to 452-477.
recommendation: Keep C0's flat cap and do not extrapolate a weak developed gradient. Any uplift should come only from a credibility-weighted emerging offset for E02 and E04, validated by grouped CV within 2023. The region correction in C2a was already rejected.

field: Fields missing in about 12% of emerging rows: days_unoccupied, smoke_alarms, marital_status, household_size, years_at_address, distance_to_river_km, soil_type, roof_type, energy_rating, occupation, security_level, high_value_items, vehicle_age, engine_size_cc, overnight_parking
finding: Missingness is consistent with missing completely at random (MCAR): it is independent across fields, the same for new business and renewals, and the same in 2023 and 2025. C0 instead applies the developed MISSING relativity, learnt on 2.5% of developed rows where missingness carries a loss-cost signal of -22% to +29%.
evidence: Missing share: developed 0.025, emerging 0.116-0.124 in every split. Rows with nothing missing: 0.279 observed against 0.279 expected if fields were independent (buildings), 0.279 against 0.280 (contents), 0.249 against 0.245 (motor). Maximum absolute correlation between missing indicators: 0.021. Share of rows with any field missing in test2025, new business against renewals: 0.720/0.721, 0.723/0.722, 0.755/0.750. C0 rate on missing rows over present rows: contents distance_to_river 1.183 and high_value_items 0.851; buildings distance 1.099 and soil 0.940; motor 0.97-1.01. Developed raw loss cost, missing over present: buildings 0.86-1.29, contents 0.78-1.20, motor 0.87-1.10. In fit2023 the A/E for missing rows rests on only 36-66 claim rows per field in buildings and contents, so it is too noisy to read.
recommendation: For a field missing completely at random, average C0's prediction over that field's emerging distribution (multiple imputation from the emerging conditional distribution, then average the predictions) instead of using the developed MISSING level. The rejected approach was a single fill from developed medians, which is a different method.

finding: Occupation can be made portable. The 80 raw values are 20 jobs, each in case and trailing-space variants and with an optional 'Self-employed ' prefix. After normalisation, every emerging row maps to one of the developed market's 20 jobs. PORTABLE_DROP excludes occupation because only about half of rows match exactly.
evidence: Raw values: 80. After trimming and lower-casing: 40. After also stripping the 'Self-employed' prefix: 20, matching developed jobs 100%. Exact raw match: 0.498 of non-missing rows. The prefix appears on 0.101 of non-missing rows. Missing share: 0.12. PSI fit2023->test2025: 0.014-0.016.
recommendation: Normalise to a job with 20 levels, which takes the developed relativities, plus a self_employed flag, which has no developed analogue and is for emerging-fitted components only. This is a candidate C0 variation; check it by CV within 2023.

finding: The depth of claim history differs by year because the emerging data begin in 2023, so a model fitted on 2023 sees no variation in these fields. In 2025, new business has no history and renewals have about twice the 2024 depth.
evidence: Share of rows with own-history exposure above 0: fit2023 0.000 / 0.017 / 0.074 (maximum 0-0.99 years); A2024 0.81-0.86; test2025 0.23-0.24 (new business 0.000, renewals 0.96-1.00). Mean renewal history: 2025 1.55-1.68 years, A2024 0.88-0.97. 22.8% of 2025 buildings exposure lies above the fit2023 maximum. PSI fit2023->A2024 for h_own_expo: 8.6. prior_claims_5y is stable (share above 0: 0.23).
recommendation: Use history only through a credibility formula whose weight depends on history exposure (as C4 did), never as a fitted feature from 2023. prior_claims_5y is the stable history field.

field: f_*_band quantile bands (rain, wildfire, hail, wind, freeze, dry, temperature, river, elevation, sum insured), z_log_si
finding: sql/08 builds the cut-points from each market's own training rows, so the same band label covers different values in each market. For the emerging market those training rows are 2023 plus 2024, including B2024 covariates (no outcomes). C0 contents is unaffected because it uses raw elevation, raw distance and log_si.
evidence: Upper value of the lowest bands, developed against emerging: f_rain_band 740/855/938 against 1141/1217/1280; f_wildfire_band 0.00/0.05/0.10 against 0.36/0.44/0.49; f_si_band 18.6k/24.1k against 17.2k/21.9k. PSI developed->fit2023 on the band labels is 0.01-0.25, against 1.0-5.9 on the raw values. z_log_si has mean and standard deviation 0/1 in both markets, yet mean log_si is 10.537 (developed) against 10.459 (emerging), about 8% apart.
recommendation: Before any use across markets or any transfer of developed relativities, rebuild bands and the standardisation on common developed cut-points. For a strictly 2023-only fit, recompute the emerging bands on fit2023 rows.

finding: Correction to the brief: the broker share is a feature of the emerging market, not a 2025 shift. New business in 2025 is no more broker-placed than new business in 2023. The difference from the developed market is large, but no levels are unseen.
evidence: Broker share: fit2023 0.702, test2025 0.699, developed 0.251. PSI fit2023->test2025: 0.000; PSI developed->fit2023: 1.11-1.13. Broker share of new business: fit2023 0.68-0.71, test2025 0.70. Rows that are both new business and broker: about 53% of 2025, not 77%.
recommendation: Suitable as it is. C0's channel relativities are applied to a different mix, so check the channel A/E within 2023 rather than assuming a 2025 broker effect.

finding: There is no sign of a broker-transfer artefact: the distribution is the same for new business and renewals in every market and year. Its only signal is a weak loading at 0 days.
evidence: 10th/50th/90th percentiles are 0/13/27 everywhere (2023 new business median 12-14). PSI is at most 0.002. In the developed market, 0-day rows have relative loss cost 1.06-1.12 and C0 in-sample A/E 1.06-1.10.
recommendation: Suitable as it is (stable). It is low value; no special treatment needed.

finding: It equals tenure exactly and is 0 exactly when the policy is new business. Its shift is the new-business mix; out-of-range values are trivial.
evidence: PSI fit2023->test2025: 2.14. Share of 2025 exposure above the fit2023 maximum (17 against 15): 0.021-0.022. No developed value is exceeded.
recommendation: Keep one of renewal_count, tenure or new_business as the encoding, not several, and cap at the fit2023 maximum.

field: Other C0 numeric and categorical inputs (sum_insured, elevation_m, distance_to_river_km, year_built, log_si, motor ncb_years, years_licensed, vehicle_age, vehicle_value_group, age bands, marketing_segment, other categoricals)
finding: Apart from customer_since_year and wildfire, everything is within the developed training range. No categorical level is unseen against either the developed market or fit2023. Age band and segment move only because of the new-business mix.
evidence: Share of 2025 exposure above the developed maximum or below the minimum: 0 for every motor and contents C0 input, and 0 for buildings sum insured, elevation, distance, year built and hail (hail above developed p99: 0.208 in 2023, 0.077 in 2025). Contents GLM levels merged into OTHER: 0.3-0.35% of exposure, the same as in the developed market. Motor vehicle_age missing 0.118-0.122 against 0.025, C0 ratio 1.007. PSI fit2023->test2025: age band 0.063-0.064, segment 0.091-0.097, years_licensed 0.067.
recommendation: No action needed beyond the treatment of missing values.

field: weather: hail_days, wind_exposure_index, freezing_days, dry_summer_index, rainfall_mm, mean_temperature_c, x_clay_dry, x_fz3_rain
finding: These are realised weather for the row's own year, so large year-to-year PSI is expected and the 2025 values are provided. The emerging climate differs from the developed one, but only wildfire leaves the developed range in volume.
evidence: PSI fit2023->A2024: 0.03-0.74; PSI fit2023->test2025: 0.23-0.50. Exposure-weighted means, fit2023 / A2024 / test2025 against developed 2021-24: rainfall 1384/1377/1251 against 980-1144; temperature 15.3/15.8/14.2 against 12.2-13.1; dry summer 0.68/0.71/0.61 against 0.47-0.59; hail 13.9/17.1/11.4 against 5.6-6.8. Share above the developed maximum is at most 0.005 for every weather field except wildfire. x_fz3_rain treats a missing flood zone as zone 3 or above, but flood-zone missingness is 0.028-0.030 in emerging against 0.029 developed, so the treatment is consistent.
recommendation: Keep as C0 does. Remember that relativities at the developed tail stay flat.

field: Cleaning rules (year_built, sum_insured, exposure, construction_type, elevation units, customer_id)
finding: The developed-market fixes also apply to the emerging data and are applied, and no emerging-specific unit problem was found.
evidence: year_built 1900 placeholder: 3.1-3.2% of emerging rows, all replaced. Sum insured ×1000 errors rescaled: 0.20-0.23%. Exposure recomputed: 0.5-0.65% (0% in test). After mapping construction codes, shares match the developed market: brick 0.697-0.702 against 0.700, timber 0.120-0.121 against 0.121, non_standard 0.100-0.102 against 0.099, stone 0.079 against 0.080. Emerging regions E01-E06 have elevation maxima of 57.7-60.0 (only developed R11, at 196.9, was recorded in feet). Motor customer_id needed padding on 10% of developed rows and 0% of emerging rows.
recommendation: None needed.

finding: Regions E01-E06 have no developed analogue, but they are stable within the emerging market and every level seen in 2025 is seen in 2023.
evidence: Unseen against the developed market: 100%. PSI fit2023->test2025: 0.000-0.003. Unseen against fit2023: 0.
recommendation: Use only in emerging-fitted or offset components; never map to developed relativities.

finding: The incumbent's relative pricing of new business against renewals did not change in 2025. Gender exists only in the emerging market and is stable.
evidence: Earned premium over C0, new business / renewals: buildings 0.778/0.804 in 2023, 0.765/0.788 in 2025; contents 1.031/1.096 and 1.034/1.084; motor 0.904/0.979 and 0.932/1.061. Correlation of log premium with log C0: 0.35-0.57. Share female: 0.499-0.511 in every split; developed gender is 100% missing.
recommendation: Leave both out of the technical model unless the owner decides otherwise. Gender cannot be carried over from the developed market.

field: credit_band, date_of_birth, policyholder_age, driver_age, annual_mileage, telematics_opt_in, telematics_score, f_age_band, f_credit
finding: These fields are absent in the emerging market by construction and are already excluded from C0.
evidence: Missing in emerging: 1.000. PSI developed->emerging: 9-18.
recommendation: Keep them excluded. Age enters only through the age bands.

finding: The field is claim-driven in emerging training, exactly as D-04 found in the developed market. In the 2025 test rows it is a different variable: pure Poisson noise with no link to exposure, line or risk. So it is both leakage in training and shifted in test.
evidence: Emerging 2023 mean contacts per row (buildings/contents/motor): no claim 0.452/0.436/0.438; one claim 3.05/2.91/2.99; two or more claims 5.84/5.56/6.05. Developed 2021-24: 0.417/0.412/0.405, then 2.96/2.96/2.96, then 5.62/5.69/5.87. C0 A/E on 2023 for rows with 0 contacts: 0.002/0.000/0.003 (only 1/1/4 claims on 6,725/8,593/9,975 exposure); for 3+ contacts: 15.3/14.6/4.70. test2025: mean 0.398/0.399/0.400 per row in every line. Distribution 0/1/2/3+ is 0.672/0.267/0.053/0.008 against Poisson(0.40) at 0.671/0.268/0.053/0.008. Flat across exposure bands (0.389-0.407; in 2023 claim-free rows it rises from 0.11-0.12 to 0.49-0.51) and across C0-rate quintiles (0.39-0.41). Share with 3+ contacts: 2025 0.8% in each line; 2023 3.6%/2.9%/10.0%. Contacts per exposure: 2025 0.440/0.448/0.458; 2023 all rows 0.618/0.576/0.985; 2023 claim-free rows 0.501/0.491/0.510.
recommendation: Keep the D-04 exclusion. Extend it to every derived form (contents f_cs_contacts), to premium or propensity models, to missing-value imputation and to any segmentation or clustering. A model using this field would treat almost every 2025 row as claim-free.

finding: This is a post-period outcome. The insurer's decline decision is driven by claims, and the field is 100% missing in test2025. C0 does not use it (checked against meta.json feature lists).
evidence: Emerging 2023 'declined_by_insurer' rows (buildings/contents/motor): 1.052/1.057/1.489 claims per exposure, against 0.040/0.033/0.181 for 'renewed'. C0 A/E 53.2/56.8/36.8. These rows carry 59/19/149 of 2023's 519/491/3,557 claims (11.4%/3.9%/4.2%). Developed: 1.11/1.15/1.36 against 0.038/0.039/0.131 for renewed. test2025 missing share 1.000 in every line.
recommendation: Never use it as a feature, filter, weight or stratifier. Do not drop 'declined_by_insurer' rows from fitting: they hold a material share of claims (11% for buildings), and dropping them would bias both the level and the relativities.

finding: On emerging 2023 the premium ranks risk reasonably on its own, but it adds nothing over C0. Every out-of-fold premium/C0 term is at or below zero, both in emerging and in the developed market. D-05 costs nothing measurable, and premium is not a route to closing the gap to the leader.
evidence: 2023 level-matched D2 (buildings/contents/motor): C0 0.0690/0.0864/0.0361 (pooled 0.1149); premium alone 0.0410/0.0318/0.0315 (pooled 0.0942). C0 A/E by exposure-weighted quintile of premium/C0 annual rate, lowest to highest: buildings 1.31/0.65/0.45/0.97/1.63 (U-shaped; 95% customer-bootstrap intervals as wide as 0.66-2.21); contents 1.06/1.18/0.87/0.86/0.82 (the opposite direction to an informative premium); motor 0.89/1.00/1.06/1.01/1.18 (expected direction, intervals overlap: 0.78-1.01 against 0.89-1.62). Out-of-fold gain of C0 x f(log premium/C0), 5 customer folds within 2023: quadratic -0.0108 [95% -0.0233, +0.0015] / -0.0047 [-0.0090, -0.0008] / -0.0020 [-0.0073, +0.0039]; linear -0.0148 / -0.0038 / -0.0007 [-0.0052, +0.0042]; 5 bands -0.0141 / -0.0091 / -0.0033. Pooled 0.1096 against C0 0.1149. Buildings fold slopes changed sign (-0.12 to +0.27). Developed 2023, over in-sample C0: -0.0005 / -0.0002 / -0.0082.
recommendation: Keep D-05 and spend no more search budget on written_premium as a ranking signal. If it is shown at all, label it a diagnostic.

finding: The 2025 new business is almost all written in January, so its rows are close to a full year. Training new business starts through the year as part-year rows. The NB effect any model learns therefore comes from Feb-Dec part-year starts. In the developed market, January-start NB is if anything slightly worse than other NB. Weak evidence; not tested out of sample.
evidence: Share of 2025 NB rows starting in January (buildings/contents/motor): 0.914/0.901/0.883 (0.958/0.951/0.941 of NB exposure; median start 9 January). Same share in 2023 emerging: 0.074/0.071/0.075; developed 2022-24: 0.080/0.079/0.077. Mean exposure per NB row: 2025 0.92/0.90/0.88; 2023 0.48/0.47/0.46; developed 0.48/0.47/0.46. Share of rows starting 1 January: 2023 0.847/0.836/0.814; 2025 0.231/0.225/0.222. Share of rows under one year of exposure: 2025 0.817/0.827/0.832; 2023 0.186/0.212/0.251. Developed January-start NB against Feb-Dec NB: frequency 0.0535 vs 0.0470 / 0.0469 vs 0.0463 / 0.1983 vs 0.1854; in-sample C0 A/E 1.12 vs 1.05 / 1.09 vs 0.98 / 1.06 vs 1.01 (340/296/1,632 claims in the January cells).
recommendation: Treat the 2025 NB book as full-year January business when setting any NB adjustment or level. Before relying on an NB uplift learned from training, test an NB x start-month effect on developed data out of sample. Contents C0's seasonal exposure (D-22) will weight these rows differently from the training NB, so check it on the 2025 profile.

line: buildings (C0 XGBoost only; contents and motor C0 are GLMs that do not use it)
finding: The field is consistent and is known before inception, but its meaning is tied to the calendar year. renewal_count = yr - customer_since_year in every row of every split. In the developed training data (2006-2024), the value 2024 meant '2024 new business'. In 2025 it means tenure-1 renewals, and 2025 is above the developed maximum. The A2024 explore score cannot show this, because in 2024 the meaning still matches developed. Effect on C0 not quantified: no saved model.
evidence: renewal_count == yr - customer_since_year: share 1.0000 in fit2023, A2024 and test2025, all lines. NB <=> renewal_count 0 <=> customer_since_year == yr: 1.0000. Same policy: renewal_count rises by exactly +1 a year; customer_since_year unchanged in 100% of cases. No dependence on renewal_decision (mean difference 0.0). Developed range 2006-2024. 2025 buildings exposure: 76.8% at 2025 (above the developed maximum), 4.2% at 2024 (tenure 1), 19.0% at 2023 or earlier. A2024: 9.5% at 2024, all of it new business.
recommendation: In any refit, replace customer_since_year with tenure (renewal_count) or drop it; it is redundant. To settle C0's exposure, predict the 2025 buildings rows with customer_since_year shifted by -1 (the 2024 meaning) and compare predictions on the 4.2% tenure-1 exposure.

finding: written_premium is the annual premium in force for the row, not the premium for the period. c0 is a per-row expected cost with exposure inside it. Within a year a policy can have several rows carrying different (mid-term re-rated) annual premiums. No missing or non-positive values in any split.
evidence: Slope of log premium on log exposure among part-year rows: buildings -0.002/+0.023/+0.001 (fit2023/A2024/test2025), contents -0.012/-0.004/-0.013, motor +0.006/+0.009/+0.022; controlling for log C0 annual rate, -0.011 to +0.008. Median premium flat across exposure bands (buildings 2023: 230.6/227.7/232.0/230.5/230.7). Slope of log c0 on log exposure: 0.956-1.011. Missing 0.0 and <=0 0.0 in every split. Policies with more than one row: 0% carry a single premium across their rows (13,735/17,910/25,469 such policies).
recommendation: Any premium-based quantity must use period premium = written_premium x exposure_plain, or compare written_premium with the annual rate c0/exposure_plain. Never use written_premium as a period amount or as an exposure measure.

finding: The 2025 book, the broker new business included, is priced on the same tariff as 2023-24, with a near-uniform rate increase of about 4% a year. A premium model fitted on 2023 covariates explains 96-97% of log premium. Out of time, its residual is the same across NB and channel, apart from a persistent 3-6% lower price for comparison-site NB, present in every year. The book-level premium/C0 ratio falls in 2025, but not through a change of basis; it moves with mix, where C0 and the tariff disagree.
evidence: Premium model: XGBoost on log premium, 2023 only, rounds chosen by customer-grouped CV. CV R2 0.968/0.959/0.961 (RMSE 0.110/0.083/0.084 against SD 0.617/0.409/0.421). Mean residual for renewals: 2024 +0.042/+0.044/+0.041; 2025 +0.092/+0.080/+0.082. 2025 broker NB residual 0.0919/0.0790/0.0821 against the 2025 renewal anchor 0.0919/0.0804/0.0815. Comparison-site NB relative to its year mean: 2023 -0.018/-0.033/-0.030; 2024 -0.050/-0.095/-0.037; 2025 -0.026/-0.058/-0.034. Residual RMSE widens out of time: 2025 broker NB 0.164/0.115/0.119 against 2023 CV 0.110/0.083/0.084. Exposure-weighted premium/C0 for broker NB, 2023/2024/2025: buildings 0.788/0.800/0.775; contents 1.053/1.065/1.049; motor 0.916/0.927/0.943. Book level: buildings 0.802/0.790/0.770; contents 1.092/1.090/1.045; motor 0.973/1.015/0.956. Same-policy premium change, geometric 2023->24 and 2024->25: buildings 1.062 and 1.061; contents 1.059 and 1.055; motor 0.994 and 0.998 (medians 1.020 and 1.024). Broker NB is 53.5%/53.8%/53.8% of 2025 exposure.
recommendation: No basis adjustment is needed for 2025 beyond the incumbent's rate change: about +8-9% in log terms from 2023 to 2025 by the premium model; same-policy +12.2%/+11.3% for buildings/contents. Allow for the persistent comparison-site NB discount, and for a tariff that 2023 does not fully reproduce in 2025 (wider residuals).

finding: No evidence that the premium carries the row's own claims. The part of the premium the covariates do not explain is unrelated to claims, and mid-term re-rating after a claim does not go up (no claim loading). Almost all the premium is explained by observed rating factors, including region, credit and occupation.
evidence: Out-of-fold premium-model residual (SD 0.111/0.084/0.084): claims per exposure across residual quintiles 0.040-0.052 / 0.031-0.039 / 0.178-0.199; C0 A/E not monotone (motor 0.96/0.95/1.12/0.94/1.03). Developed log premium change at a same-year mid-term break after a claim, against no claim: buildings -0.133 (SE 0.042, n 522), contents -0.001 (SE 0.009, n 667), motor -0.019 (SE 0.004, n 4,003). Emerging 2023 too small to read (n 13/17/133). Premium-model gain shares: buildings x_fz3_rain 0.43, flood_zone 0.33, sum_insured 0.12; contents log sum insured 0.59 + 0.24; motor driver_age_band 0.64, ncb_years 0.15; region 0.01-0.04.
recommendation: No leakage action needed beyond D-05. Whatever risk information the premium holds is available directly from the raw rating fields.

finding: discount_applied is a fixed function of channel x new business, with the same rule in the developed market and in every emerging year. It is unrelated to claims and is not post-inception information. It is redundant with channel and NB, so it adds no information about the 2025 broker book.
evidence: Rule, with SD 0 in developed: renewals broker 0, comparison 0, direct 0.05; NB broker 0, comparison 0.10, direct 0.05. 2023 C0 A/E at 0 and 0.05: 0.985/1.059 (buildings), 1.007/0.976 (contents), 1.003/0.907 (motor). Share at 0.10: 2023 0.6%, 2025 3.8% (more comparison-site NB).
recommendation: Safe to use, but redundant: prefer channel x NB directly. Buildings C0's XGBoost uses it, which is harmless.

finding: The field looks like uniform noise from 0 to 30 days, identical across years, NB and renewals, and channels. Not shifted in 2025, no link to claims, no sign of post-inception information.
evidence: Quartiles 4/13/21-22, minimum 0, maximum 30, mean 13.0-13.5 in every split x NB cell (2025 13.1-13.2). 2023 frequency across bands: 0.036-0.049 / 0.023-0.041 / 0.178-0.196. Mean days by claims band: 13.2 vs 13.2 (buildings), 13.3 vs 13.8 (contents), 13.2 vs 13.0 (motor). Developed similar (13.0-13.2).
recommendation: No leakage. Consider dropping it from tree models as a noise feature; buildings C0's XGBoost uses it.

finding: renewal_count is consistent, known before inception and defined the same way in every year. Only its distribution shifts, because of the 2025 NB share.
evidence: NB rows all have renewal_count 0 and renewals none; rises by exactly +1 per policy-year (6,004/7,461/10,053 policies, 2023->24). Median 7 (2023), 6 (2024), 0 (2025); NB share 0.120/0.117/0.121 (2023) against 0.760/0.761/0.760 (2025). 2023 C0 A/E by count is noisy and not monotone (motor count 0: 1.81, then 0.66-1.22).
recommendation: Suitable as the tenure feature, in place of customer_since_year.

finding: compulsory_excess is constant within each line in every split and in the developed market. It carries no information and so no leakage.
evidence: 350 for buildings and contents, 250 for motor, in 100% of rows in fit2023, A2024, test2025 and developed 2021-24; the same mean in every claims band.
recommendation: Drop it; it can contribute nothing.

finding: The first observed year of each market (emerging 2023, developed 2021) has no customer lapses and no mid-year cancellations. Later years have both. So 2023 part-year exposure comes only from NB starts and mid-term changes. Developed data shows lapse and cancellation are not related to claims, so the expected bias in rates is small.
evidence: Emerging 2023: renewed 95.8%/94.5%/92.2%, mid-term change 3.8%/5.4%/7.4%, declined 0.45%/0.11%/0.49%, lapsed 0, cancelled 0. A2024: lapsed 10.1%/10.1%/9.4%, cancelled 4.6%/4.8%/5.0%. Developed 2021: lapsed and cancelled 0; 2022-24: 9.3-9.8% and 4.7-5.0%. Developed frequency, lapsed / cancelled / renewed: buildings 0.0365/0.0409/0.0377; contents 0.0384/0.0382/0.0385; motor 0.1295/0.1248/0.131.
recommendation: Treat it as a construction artefact. Do not read the 2023 to 2024 change in the exposure profile as a change in risk.

finding: exposure_raw is corrupt in a few training rows (days rather than years, or values just above 1). exposure_plain is clean and equals days/365 exactly in every split.
evidence: Rows with exposure_raw > 1: buildings 0.52% (2023) and 0.39% (A2024), motor 0.49% and 0.35%, including 19-20 rows at 365; 0 in test2025. Maximum |exposure_plain - days/365| = 0 in every split. Contents has no exposure_raw column.
recommendation: Use exposure_plain only, as the harness does.

finding: No A2024 outcome was read and nothing was scored on A2024 with the harness. Outcomes came only from emerging fit2023 and developed rows; A2024 and test2025 were used for covariates only (premium, contacts, dates and so on). The held-back half was not touched.
evidence: Configurations scored on A2024: 0. Scripts: <a31 scratch>/data/d2_premium_leakage/s1_basis.py to s8_contacts_test.py, plus util.py. s3_out.txt and s4_out.txt are aggregate logs; deleting them was refused by the permission system, so they remain.
recommendation: No search correction is needed for this task.

finding: This was analysis only. No configuration was scored on A2024, no A2024 outcome was read, and the held-back half was neither searched for nor opened. Every outcome-based check uses emerging fit2023 rows or developed rows. The one exception is the pack file ev_w1_transfer_by_factor.csv, which the brief named: its 2024 rows pool both 2024 halves, including the held-back half, so it is reported descriptively and used for no choice.
evidence: A2024 configurations scored: 0. Scripts and aggregate outputs are in <a31 scratch>/data/d3_cross_market/ (p1-p8 *.py; out/*.csv and *.log). Compute was about 2 minutes in total.
recommendation: If anyone selects factors from the 2024 columns of ev_w1_transfer_by_factor.csv, record it: those columns already contain the confirmation half.

finding: Identifiers collide across the two markets. A plain union would merge distinct customers in customer-grouped CV and mis-join history and address tables.
evidence: Share of emerging cache rows whose ID also appears in developed: row_id 49.9% (buildings), 100% (motor), 0% (contents); customer_id 0.24-0.34%; address_id 2.6-3.1%; policy_id 0.2-0.3%.
recommendation: Prefix every key with the market before any union, grouped fold assignment or history join, and assert uniqueness afterwards.

finding: The two markets differ in level, and the components move in opposite directions. Frequency and severity both differ, and the shift in the cost tail undermines currency-based thresholds. A pooled model without market-specific level terms would misprice every emerging row. excess_dev in the cache is the part above the 1m cap, not the 50k large-claim split.
evidence: 2023 like for like (developed 2023 against emerging fit2023). Cost per exposure-year: buildings 433.8 vs 514.7 (x1.19), contents 117.2 vs 91.3 (x0.78), motor 604.8 vs 444.8 (x0.74). Motor frequency 140.2 vs 188.6 per 1,000 (x1.35); motor median claim-row severity 1,677 vs 1,066 (x0.64). Contents frequency 41.1 vs 34.8. Share of cost on rows above 50k: motor 22.6% vs 7.2%, buildings 37.5% vs 51.6%, contents 2.8% vs 0%. excess_dev sum: developed motor 11.82m (the 12.55m claim less the 1m cap); emerging 0.
recommendation: Give each line a market intercept, separately for frequency and severity where the model allows. Rescale currency thresholds for emerging (50k emerging is roughly 82k developed at a severity ratio of 0.61). Rebuild the 50k split from claims rather than from excess_dev. Model year effects by market, since developed covers 2021-24 and emerging 2023-24.

finding: Developed data would swamp emerging in an unweighted pool: the pooled fit would in effect be the developed model.
evidence: Emerging fit2023 is 1.75% of pooled buildings rows, 2.15% of contents rows and 2.16% of motor rows (exposure shares 1.9%, 2.3%, 2.3%). Developed rows number 707,726, 721,617 and 979,968.
recommendation: Use C0 or developed shapes as an offset or prior with emerging corrections, or give emerging rows explicit case weights chosen by grouped CV within 2023. Do not pool at equal weight.

field: sum_insured, voluntary_excess, compulsory_excess, vehicle_value_group, engine_size_cc, seats, bedrooms, flood_zone, elevation_m, year_built, written_premium
finding: The shared numeric rating fields use the same units and scales in both markets, and the cleaning rules were applied identically. No unit conversion is needed. Emerging claims are cheaper at the same sum insured, but that is a level effect, not a units effect.
evidence: Voluntary excess takes {0,250,500,1000} with shares 50/30/15/5 (home) and 40/30/20/10 (motor) in both markets. Compulsory excess is 350 (home) and 250 (motor) in both. Vehicle_value_group runs 1-20 with near-identical shares (KS 0.016). engine_size_cc runs 500/600-3,600 (KS 0.016). Buildings sum insured median 223k vs 228k (KS 0.027); contents 38.9k vs 35.7k (KS 0.068). The sum-insured /1,000 fix touched 1,395 developed rows (0.20%) and 147 emerging rows (0.20%), with the same rule. Elevation after cleaning is capped at 60 m in both (KS 0.004-0.011; developed raw maximum 197 m, emerging raw maximum 60 m). year_built KS 0.008. written_premium is on the same scale (medians 217 vs 235 buildings, 127 vs 118 contents, 480 vs 501 motor); this is a diagnostic only under D-05.
recommendation: Keep the cleaned columns as they are, and add range assertions (excess value sets, VVG 1-20, elevation at most 60, sum insured below 1m after the fix) to catch future drift.

field: hail_days, wind_exposure_index, freezing_days, dry_summer_index, wildfire_index, rainfall_mm, mean_temperature_c
finding: The units match (index 0-1 or 0-10, days, mm, degrees C), but much of the emerging climate lies outside the developed support. Trees hold flat beyond the training maximum, and GLM top bands lump the tail, so developed climate relativities are extrapolated, not observed, for a large share of exposure.
evidence: wildfire_index above the developed maximum of 0.635: 23.6% of 2023 and 22.1% of 2025 buildings exposure. Above the developed p99: 55.6% (2023) and 69.7% (2025). Hail p99 is 42 days in emerging 2023-24 against 19 in developed; 20.8% of 2023 and 7.7% of 2025 exposure lie above the developed p99. Medians, developed against emerging: freezing 35 vs 20 days, dry summer 0.54 vs 0.68, rainfall 1,014 vs 1,339 mm, temperature 13.1 vs 15.4 C. KS 0.13-0.80.
recommendation: Use parametric climate terms (log-linear, with developed slopes as priors and emerging or pooled re-estimation where the audit found differences). Clip at the training minimum and maximum, and run a clamped against extrapolated sensitivity for wildfire. Do not rely on tree extrapolation beyond 0.635.

finding: The region codes do not overlap, and no emerging region is a climatic analogue of any developed region. A shared region factor would put every emerging row on an unseen level. C0 already drops region.
evidence: R01-R12 against E01-E06: 100% of emerging exposure falls on unseen levels. In developed-SD units of the seven climate means, each E region's nearest R region is 2.48-4.53 away, against a median nearest-neighbour distance of 1.56 among R regions (maximum 2.56). Region means: E wildfire 0.38-0.84 vs R 0.02-0.34; E hail 4.9-24.2 vs R 3.0-10.3.
recommendation: Never map R to E. In a joint model, region is either an emerging-only, heavily shrunk effect on top of the address and climate terms, or it is dropped.

finding: sql/08 cuts the contents band features on each market's own training quantiles and standardises z_log_si within each market. The same label or z value therefore means a different hazard or sum insured in each market. C0's contents GLM uses plain log_si and raw elevation and river distance, so it avoids this; any joint or XGB model using these columns would not.
evidence: f_hail_band q00 is 0-2 days in developed but 0-7 in emerging; q07 starts at 12 vs 27 days. The emerging f_wildfire_band q00 (0.131-0.357) spans developed q04-q07. f_si_band edges shift by about 7% (q00 upper edge 18,600 vs 17,200). z_log_si implied mean/SD: 10.537/0.5195 in developed against 10.469/0.5383 in emerging, so the same sum insured lands 0.13 SD apart.
recommendation: Rebuild every band from raw values on one set of edges (the developed edges, or pooled ones), and use log_si, never z_log_si, in anything that pools or carries relativities across markets.

finding: Both the shares and the frequency order support the CONFORM mapping BRK->brick, WOD->timber, MIX->non_standard, STN->stone. Swapping MIX and STN would contradict both. The developed raw field also needs cleaning, since it holds 11 spellings. C0's A/E by construction is within noise. The mapping remains an inference from shares and frequency order.
evidence: Raw emerging shares BRK 70.1 / WOD 12.0 / MIX 10.0 / STN 7.9%, against cleaned developed brick 70.0 / timber 12.1 / non_standard 9.9 / stone 8.0%. Frequency per 1,000, developed: brick 42.4, non_standard 59.3, stone 43.1, timber 45.5. Emerging fit2023: 40.3, 72.0, 46.8, 53.5; non_standard is highest in both, at 1.40 (developed) and 1.79 (emerging) relative to brick. Developed raw includes Brick 64.4%, W 7.1%, T 4.4%, BRICK, brick, w, t, NON_STANDARD and STONE. C0 A/E chi-square 3.9 on 3 df (p 0.27); 2023-24 correlation of log A/E -0.64.
recommendation: Keep the mapping, assert that no code is left unmapped in either market, and record the mapping as an inference.

finding: The 80 raw emerging values are the 20 developed jobs, varying only in case, a trailing space and a 'Self-employed ' prefix. After normalisation every row matches. C0 drops occupation as non-portable (56% match), yet it is a strong developed factor in motor and contents.
evidence: Normalising takes 80 values to 40 (trim and lower-case) and then to 20 (strip the self-employed prefix). Exposure matched to developed levels rises from 49.8% to 89.9% to 100%. Job-mix TVD against developed after normalisation is 0.039. Self-employed rows are 10.0% of emerging exposure, with no developed counterpart. Variants for one job: 'Teacher', 'teacher', 'Teacher ', 'Self-employed teacher'. One-way frequency chi-square per df, developed: motor 206, contents 10.9, buildings 0.81; emerging motor fit2023: 5.6.
recommendation: Normalise and re-admit occupation in any joint or portable model, with a separate emerging-only self-employed flag. The owner should know that occupation partly proxies gender (D-36).

finding: Emerging missingness looks missing completely at random. It is flat across covariates, independent across fields, unrelated to claim frequency, and leaves the observed distributions matching developed. Because it is spread over many fields, most emerging rows have at least one gap, so complete-case modelling is not viable. flood_zone is the exception: its missing rate is not elevated, and its missingness is informative in both markets.
evidence: 10-11 fields per line are missing at 11.5-12.5% in emerging against 2.5% in developed. Missing rates are flat by region (for example 0.109-0.125), channel, new business and year. Rows with at least one missing field: emerging buildings 2023-24 72.0% (72.3% expected under independence); two or more: 34.4% (34.4% expected); mean pairwise phi 0.0015, maximum 0.020. Developed rows with any missing field: 22-24%. None of 31 fit2023 frequency ratios (missing against observed) exceeds |z| 1.96; the largest is days_unoccupied at 0.74 (z -1.95). Non-missing KS against developed is at most 0.025, except vehicle_age (see below) and soil. Soil missingness is 11.6-13.0% across E regions whose clay shares run 10.5-45.1%, so the different clay share reflects region mix, not missingness. flood_zone is missing at 2.8-3.0% in both markets; frequency ratio x1.26 (z 7.1) developed, x1.76 (z 2.75) emerging buildings.
recommendation: Impute from developed conditional distributions given observed covariates, or average the prediction over the missing field. Do not use complete cases. Keep flood_zone missing as its own level.

finding: C0 applies the missing-value effects it learned on the developed 2.5% to the 12% of emerging rows that are missing completely at random. It uplifts rows with a missing river distance with no emerging support. The interaction x_clay_dry is set to 0 wherever soil is missing, so those rows are treated as non-clay for subsidence.
evidence: C0's rate for missing against observed rows, on emerging covariates: distance_to_river_km x1.112 (buildings) and x1.185 (contents); soil x0.931; energy_rating x1.038; vehicle_age x1.033; campaign_code x0.906 (buildings) and x0.787 (motor), the latter acting as a new-business proxy. Emerging fit2023 frequency ratio for missing river distance: 0.96 (z -0.29) buildings, 1.14 (z 0.97) contents. x_clay_dry is 0 on all 8,786 soil-missing buildings rows; about 35% of emerging non-missing soil is clay.
recommendation: Replace developed MISSING levels with imputation or neutral handling. Impute x_clay_dry as P(clay given E region) multiplied by dry_summer_index.

field: campaign_code, discount_applied, customer_since_year, renewal_count, h_* claim history
finding: Several fields duplicate new business, and their composition differs by market, so effects learned in developed land on different groups in emerging. The claim-history window is truncated in emerging. The buildings C0 XGB uses most of these fields.
evidence: campaign_code is present on 100% of new business in both markets, but on renewals at 20.9% (developed), 4.3% (emerging 2023-24) and 27.8% (emerging 2025). discount_applied mean on new business: 5.5% developed vs 1.75% emerging (renewals 2.0% vs 1.2%). customer_since_year is 2025 on 76% of 2025 rows, above every training maximum (2024). renewal_count median is 0 in 2025 against 6-7 in training. h_own_expo for renewals: 1.17-1.30 years developed vs 0.32-0.38 emerging 2023-24. In motor fit2023 the one new-business effect shows up four times: new business A/E 1.81 (z 4.0), campaign present 1.89, renewal_count 0 at 1.81, customer_since top band 1.47.
recommendation: Collapse these into a single new-business flag (plus 0 against 1+ renewals). Drop campaign_code, discount_applied and customer_since_year as features. Express claim history as claims per exposure with credibility on observed exposure, not as raw counts.

field: branch_id, previous_insurer, email_domain, document_preference, marketing_consent, vehicle_colour
finding: These codes share lists and distributions across markets, but their cross-market meaning cannot be verified, and on a million rows they carry no developed frequency signal. They add only noise to a joint model. The buildings C0 XGB uses the first five.
evidence: Cross-market TVD is at most 0.025. Developed one-way frequency chi-square per df ranges 0.15-3.51; 14 of 15 tests have p > 0.05 and the minimum is p 0.043 (motor document_preference). Cramér's V with region is at most 0.026 in either market, so branch is not regional. vehicle_colour has a small developed effect (0.97-1.03, chi-square per df 4.6) and none in emerging (0.27).
recommendation: Drop these fields from joint models and from any refit of the buildings XGB, or keep vehicle_colour only with heavy shrinkage.

finding: The 300 codes denote the same vehicles in both markets, so the field can be pooled. Its residual signal is modest, and emerging is too thin per model to confirm it.
evidence: The modal body type and modal fuel agree for 100% of the 300 models. Per-model mean engine size and value group correlate at 0.997 across markets. Developed one-way relativity p05-p95 is 0.89-1.11 (between-model variance 0.0045 against Poisson noise 0.0027). The developed-emerging fit2023 correlation is 0.04 at about 12 claims per model.
recommendation: Pool with strong shrinkage (a random effect or target encoding fitted on developed); no harmonisation needed.

finding: The emerging vehicle_age distribution is the developed one shifted by about +2 years, with no vehicle under 3 in any year. The emerging frequency-by-age curve also fits the developed curve better when shifted. This suggests a different age definition, or a genuinely older fleet; the data cannot tell which.
evidence: 0% of emerging rows are aged 0-2, against 6.9% of developed. KS against developed is 0.241 unshifted and 0.031 at +2 years. From age 5 upwards the shares match within 0.3 points (developed age 3: 7.3% against emerging age 5: 7.3%). The share ageing exactly one year from 2023 to 2024 is 91.9% (developed 92.5%). Poisson deviance of emerging fit2023 counts against the developed age curve: 48.6 unshifted, 33.3 shifted by -2 (23 levels).
recommendation: Test emerging vehicle_age minus 2 as a harmonisation variant in a joint model. Record it as an inference; do not adopt it without an out-of-time check.

finding: Taken together, developed motor relativities are too steep for emerging in both frequency and severity. Contents relativities, mainly the address and flood terms, are if anything too flat. Buildings shows no clear departure. This is a 2023-only, in-sample diagnostic and is untested on A2024.
evidence: Slope b in log mu = a + b log C0, with a customer bootstrap 95% interval. Motor: cost 0.65 (0.40-0.93); capped at 50k 0.79 (0.61-0.95); frequency 0.90 (0.85-0.96). Developed in-sample references: 0.86-1.07, 0.97-1.03 and 1.00-1.03. Motor per-factor transfer slopes: years_licensed 0.83±0.10, ncb 0.88±0.10, driver_age_band 0.89±0.09, marketing_segment 0.90±0.10, marital 0.69±0.20. Contents: cost 1.14 (0.99-1.31) against developed 0.90-0.97; transfer slopes f_flood_zone 1.16±0.13, elevation 1.37±0.21, river distance 1.58±0.25, log_si 1.19±0.25. Buildings: cost 1.07 (0.80-1.31); capped 0.90 (0.70-1.10) against developed 1.06-1.08.
recommendation: A joint model should allow market-specific shrinkage of the motor driver relativities and market-specific steepness for contents geography. Candidate variations to score under the A2024 protocol: C0 motor raised to a power of about 0.8, with the power chosen by grouped CV on 2023, and steeper contents flood and address terms.

field: which developed relativities hold (ev_w1_transfer_by_factor.csv, plus fit2023 row-level)
finding: On the 27 factor-by-line tables in the pack, emerging departures from C0's relativities are consistent with noise and do not repeat between years. The few genuine departures are motor new business, a buildings age-band cell, climate bands, and factors C0 lacks, such as motor fuel type.
evidence: Noise model uses the claim-row cost CV (2.92 buildings, 1.57 contents, 2.23 motor). Summed chi-square: buildings 30.7 on 31 df (p 0.48), contents 45.9 on 35 (p 0.10), motor 34.6 on 31 (p 0.30). Only 2 of 27 factors are significant pooled over years: buildings age 35-49 at 0.46, motor new business at 1.23. Median 2023-24 correlation of log A/E is -0.15 (37% positive). Positive replication only for buildings flood zone 0.58, property type 0.61, urban density 0.56, motor cover type 0.77. On fit2023 with model-based SEs, 15 of 114 tests have p < 0.05 (5.7 expected); 4 of them are the one motor new-business effect. The others: buildings wind q3 0.34 and rainfall q2 0.18; motor hail; motor fuel (hybrid 1.29, petrol 0.88; fuel is not in the C0 GLM); contents river, excess and urban.
recommendation: Carry developed shapes over as priors and spend emerging degrees of freedom only on new business by line, climate slopes, contents geography steepness and motor driver-factor shrinkage. Treat the 2023 buildings 35-49 cell as fire volatility, not a relativity.

field: channel, payment_method, cover_type, vehicle_use, body_type, fuel_type, marketing_segment
finding: Category names match exactly, so no recoding is needed. Channel mix is very different, and its strong developed signal is weak in emerging. Payment, cover and use have similar mixes and A/E within noise.
evidence: Channel shares: broker 25% -> 70%, comparison site 35% -> 5%, direct 40% -> 25% (TVD 0.45). One-way frequency chi-square per df for channel: developed 72/66/307 (buildings/contents/motor), emerging 0.34/0.31/3.49. C0 channel A/E p 0.77 (buildings) and 0.075 (motor; comparison site 1.41). Annual payment 54.9% vs 55.2%; comprehensive cover 82.1% vs 79.0%; electric vehicles 8.1% vs 2.0%; young_affluent 12.3% (developed), 17.2% (emerging 2023-24), 26.0% (2025).
recommendation: Keep developed relativities, with a shrunk market-by-channel term; treat 2025 broker business as the audit does for new business.

field: credit_band, policyholder_age, driver_age, annual_mileage, telematics_score, telematics_opt_in, gender
finding: Some fields exist in only one market: credit band, exact ages, mileage and telematics are absent in emerging, and gender is absent in developed. In a pooled tree, every emerging row would route to a missing branch learned on the developed rows.
evidence: 100% missing in emerging: credit_band, policyholder_age, driver_age, annual_mileage, telematics_opt_in and telematics_score (also 87.6% missing within developed). Gender: 100% missing in developed; 49.5-50.7% F in emerging.
recommendation: Exclude these from joint models. Use age bands (already conformed). Gender stays an emerging-only labelled diagnostic until the owner decides D-36.

finding: The developed contents exposure column is on a different per-row basis from exposure_plain, though the totals agree. The raw exposure field still contains the day-count rows in both markets.
evidence: Developed contents exposure differs from exposure_plain on 100% of rows (maximum 0.024 years, p99 0.018), with both summing to 590,859.3; emerging matches exactly. exposure_raw maximum is 365 in both markets' training data.
recommendation: Use exposure_plain as the offset and weight in both markets; never use exposure or exposure_raw.

finding: The target is internally consistent and clean. The 1m D-12 cap never binds in emerging, so excess_dev is 0 on every row and y_full equals claim_cost_dev.
evidence: max |y_full - (claim_cost_dev + excess_dev)| = 0 in both markets. Emerging fit2023/A2024: 0 NaN, 0 negative, 0 rows with claims but zero cost, 0 rows with y>0 but no reported claim, 5 motor rows with 0<y<1. Rows with excess_dev>0: 0 in emerging (largest emerging claim 361,093 reported); 3 in developed motor (11.55m excess in 2023 from the 11.89m claim). Developed: one zero-cost motor claim.
recommendation: Use y_full as it is for integrity. Ignore excess_dev in emerging, because it is degenerate there.

field: claim-to-row matching (claims vs cache n_claims, claim_cost)
finding: Claims are fully matched to rows. The only unmatched claims are dated before the policy's first period (pre-entry), and the cached targets reconcile exactly with the raw claims. Rows in 2024 end on 30 December (365-day basis), but no claims fall on 31 December 2024, so nothing is lost.
evidence: Emerging, fit2023+A2024 policies (2024-dated claims of policies with no A2024 row dropped on load). Duplicates 0. Repudiated excluded: contents 9, motor 84. Net cost <=0: 0. Recoveries > incurred: 0. Reported after 2024-12-31: 0. Unmatched: buildings 3 (19,427), contents 5 (9,584), motor 28 (63,257), all 'before first period'. Reconciliation: rows differing 0; claims 799/733/5,280; reported 8,073,849/1,940,084/11,969,207 equal on both sides. Developed: 109/84/411 duplicates removed; 67/49/293 unmatched, all before first period. Claims dated 2024-12-31: 0 in developed (138 on 2023-12-31) and none unmatched in emerging.
recommendation: No action. The period-match and repudiation filters carry over unchanged.

field: y_full development (2024 immature; developed reporting pattern)
finding: The 2024 motor target is still substantially immature. Development adds 15.4% to A2024 motor y_full, and most of it is bodily injury: reported BI claims are grossed up by x1.61 (BF). IBNR attaches only to rows that already have a reported claim. The 2023 target is close to mature.
evidence: Development factor (y_full/reported): A2024 1.182, fit2023 1.028; developed 2024 1.236, developed 2023 1.029. A2024 uplift 692,881 of 4,499,327, of which at least 476,376 sits on 75 single-peril BI rows (factor 1.613, 69% open). Other perils: TPP 1.052, own damage 1.036, glass 1.027. fit2023 BI factor 1.080. C0 scored on the A2024 reported target instead of y_full: pooled LM D2 0.11819 vs 0.12012 (motor 0.0287 vs 0.0270).
recommendation: Fit 2023 corrections on y_full as it is. If 2024 rows are used for fitting, cap on reported cost before development (as glm_lines.split_targets does) and treat the BI uplift as a level item. Development moves the ranking score by only about 0.002. Whether the 2025 truth will be developed or as-reported is not known; that is a level question.

finding: Buildings and contents 2024 development is modest. It is concentrated in subsidence and late-2024 losses, on few rows.
evidence: A2024 factor: buildings 1.052 (developed 2024 1.079); contents 1.015 (1.027). Buildings A2024 by peril: subsidence 1.729 (7 rows, 86% open), escape of water 1.070, storm 1.055, fire and flood 1.000. By loss quarter: Q3 1.11, Q4 1.12. fit2023: 1.001 and 1.001.
recommendation: Use as it is. Do not read subsidence rankings from 2024 rows.

field: large claims (exceedances of the 50k threshold), emerging vs developed
finding: Large buildings claims occur at the developed frequency at 50k, but they are about twice the size, and very large losses are 5-7 times as frequent. Measured against emerging's lower attritional severity, the tail is heavier still. Row targets are extremely concentrated.
evidence: >50k: 28 claims, 1.610 per 1,000 (95% 1.070-2.326), against developed 1.609 (950 claims, 2021-24). Mean excess over 50k: 89,733 vs 46,949. >250k: fit2023 0.352 and A2024 0.166 per 1,000, against developed 0.047-0.073. At the severity-scaled threshold (50k x 0.675 = 33,750) the rate ratio is 1.89. All emerging claims >25k are fire (28+9), flood (17+9) or subsidence (6). fit2023: 22 rows >50k hold 51.6% of cost; top 10 rows 37.4%. A2024: top row 361,093 (15.4% of the line), top 10 rows 46.9%.
recommendation: Do not fit buildings corrections on the uncapped row target. Cap at 50k, or at about 34k (severity-scaled), with the excess spread back pro rata to C0 or modelled as a separate large-loss/fire component.

finding: The 2023 buildings target is dominated by fire. E02 alone contributes a fifth of the year's cost. Against C0, the 2023 one-way 'signals' for region and age band are artefacts of where the fires fell, and they disappear once fire is removed. The E02 spike is not explained by the wildfire index, because E04 has a higher index and an ordinary fire rate (inference from 2023 only).
evidence: Fire is 55.1% of 2023 buildings y_full (3,223,096 of 5,853,659): 49 claims, 4.31 per 1,000 (developed 1.68-2.06), 9 total losses. E02 2023: 18 fire claims, 8.81 per 1,000 vs 3.32 in other regions, 1,224,989 = 20.9% of 2023 buildings y_full. One-way A/E vs C0 on 2023: E02 1.588 raw, 1.021 without fire; age 35-49 0.317 raw, 0.851 without fire. Heterogeneity chi-square: age band 27.1/4 (p<0.001) raw vs 5.4/4 (p=0.25) without fire; region 7.7/5 (p=0.17) vs 3.6/5 (p=0.60). Mean wildfire index in 2023: E02 0.746, E04 0.865 (fire 3.97 per 1,000). E02 test 2025 index: 0.754.
recommendation: Separate fire from the other buildings perils: fire level pooled over 2023-24 and driven by the wildfire index, with corrections fitted on the non-fire target. Alternatively, cap at 50k or less with spread-back. Do not adopt region or age corrections fitted on raw 2023 buildings.

field: estimation noise of corrections on 2023, by target treatment
finding: Capping or removing fire cuts the sampling error of one-way corrections by a factor of 2-3.
evidence: Median customer-bootstrap SE of log A/E (300 reps), region: raw 0.304, cap 100k 0.181, cap 50k 0.137, cap 25k 0.094, without fire 0.100, without fire and capped at 50k 0.092. New business: 0.251 / 0.182 / 0.148 / 0.097 / 0.126. Age band: 0.280 / 0.186 / 0.137 / 0.086 / 0.100.
recommendation: Tune ridge corrections (the C2a/C2b type) on the capped target. Part of the earlier 'no significant gain' result may be noise from the uncapped target.

field: large claims (exceedances of the 50k threshold), emerging vs developed
finding: In developed-currency terms the 50k threshold sits too high for emerging motor. Rescaled by the A30 severity ratio of 0.612, emerging exceedance matches developed. There is no catastrophic emerging claim.
evidence: >50k: 8 claims, 0.276 per 1,000 (95% 0.119-0.544), vs developed 0.751 (ratio 0.37). >30,600 (=50k x 0.612): ratio 0.97. >15,300 vs developed >25k: ratio 1.06. Mean excess over 50k: 35,815 vs 65,306. Largest emerging claim 136,767 reported (row 155,276), vs developed 11,894,277. Developed >50k by year: 1.03, 1.00, 0.63, 0.37 per 1,000, falling partly because recent years are immature. fit2023 rows: excess over 50k 3.6% of cost, top 10 rows 9.3%.
recommendation: For emerging, use about 30k as the large/attritional split and the cap for correction fitting, not 50k.

finding: The 2023 motor new-business excess over C0 comes mostly from a handful of large bodily-injury rows. The frequency excess is modest.
evidence: fit2023 new-business A/E vs C0: raw 1.808, cap 100k 1.687, cap 50k 1.488, cap 25k 1.339; renewals 0.934. Six new-business rows >25k (494,985) are 43.0% of new-business cost; excluding rows >25k, new business 1.033 vs renewals 0.836 (relative 1.24, against 1.94 raw). New business has 6 of 26 rows >25k on 6.4% of exposure. Frequency A/E for new business, relative to the overall rate, is 1.08-1.21 across exposure bands.
recommendation: Fit any new-business correction on a capped target (about 30k), preferably split into frequency and severity, and shrink it towards the developed prior. The raw 2023 A/E would misprice a 2025 book that is 77% new business.

finding: Contents has no large-claim problem. Capping makes no material difference.
evidence: No emerging claim >50k (max 44,269), vs developed 0.030 per 1,000. >19,700 (severity-scaled 25k): 10 claims, 0.464 per 1,000 (95% 0.222-0.853) vs 0.305 (ratio 1.52). fit2023 top row is 2.7% of cost, top 10 rows 18.1%. Capping at 25k changes one-way A/E by no more than 0.16 (E04: 2.071 to 1.913) and median SE from 0.195 to 0.188. Development: A2024 1.015.
recommendation: Use y_full as it is. A 25k cap is harmless but unnecessary.

finding: Exposure is suitable. There are no zero, negative or over-1 values; every row is a calendar-year slice measured in days/365; and claims are roughly proportional to exposure. Mid-year renewal terminations are more common from the second year of each book, and the 2025 test book has the same pattern as 2024.
evidence: Emerging and developed: NaN 0, <=0 0, >1 0. Minimum 0.0027 (1 day). 100% of rows fall within one calendar year. D-01 exposure fixes: buildings 82 (fit2023) + 36 (A2024), motor 129 + 70, test 0. Renewals starting 1 January: 92-96%. Full-year renewal rows: buildings fit2023 92.4%, A2024 75.7%, test 75.9% (developed 2021 92.4%, 2022-24 75.7-75.8%). Developed claim frequency per exposure for partial rows vs full-year: renewals 0.95-1.27, new business 0.91-1.17. The elevated value (buildings renewals at exposure <=0.25: 1.24-1.27) is consistent with winter seasonality.
recommendation: Use exposure_plain as it is, never exposure_raw. No short-exposure adjustment is needed beyond seasonality.

finding: Training new business incepts mid-year and runs about half a year, mostly in the second half. 2025 new business incepts in early January and runs almost a full year. Because buildings claims are winter-heavy, a new-business relativity measured on training carries a small seasonal bias when applied to 2025.
evidence: Median inception day of new business: training 184-196, test 2025 9. Mean new-business exposure: training 0.46-0.49, test 0.88-0.92. Share of new-business exposure in July-December: training about 75%, test 52%. 96-97% of test new-business partial exposure incepts in Q1. Seasonal index of the exposure profile (developed monthly weights; buildings December-February frequency 1.30-1.34 x average): buildings frequency 0.976 (training new business) vs 0.9935 (2025 new business), +1.8%; cost 0.979 vs 0.997, +1.9%. Contents frequency 0.986 vs 0.9975, +1.2%; cost about 0. Motor about -0.3%.
recommendation: Treat this as a level or new-business-factor adjustment of no more than 2%, or use month-weighted exposure when estimating new-business corrections. It does not matter for ranking.

finding: The developed contents model was fitted on seasonal exposure (D-22), but for emerging rows C0 multiplies by plain exposure. The inconsistency is small.
evidence: Monthly weights recovered exactly from the developed exposure (max error 5e-13): Jan 1.108, Feb 1.127 ... Nov 0.943, Dec 1.066. Seasonal/plain exposure: training new business 0.986, renewals 1.000, test new business 0.9975; per-row range 0.94-1.13. fit2023 new-business A/E: 1.005 on C0 as it is, 1.019 on seasonal exposure.
recommendation: Optional consistency fix: scale contents C0 by seasonal/plain exposure. Negligible for ranking.

field: score dependence on the largest claims (C0)
finding: The A2024 score rests heavily on a few claims, mostly buildings fire and flood. Moving C0 by 10% on just the 10 largest rows shifts pooled D2 by about 0.004, which is more than most gains claimed so far. The buildings level-matched scale is also fragile.
evidence: C0 pooled level-matched D2 0.12012. Customer bootstrap (1,000): sd 0.0150, 95% 0.0941-0.1534. The top 10 rows (0.034% of 29,649) carry 10.6% of null deviance and 27.3% of C0's gain over the null; top 50 rows 45.0%; top 100 rows 49.0%. Dropping the top rows pooled: top 1 +0.0002, top 3 -0.0043, top 10 -0.0190 (buildings 0.109 to 0.052), top 50 -0.0270. Capping the row target: 100k -0.0016, 50k -0.0066, 25k -0.0150. C0 moved by x1.1 or x0.9 on the top-10 rows only: +0.0038 / -0.0044 (top row alone: +0.0011 / -0.0013); on 10 random claim rows: +0.0001 (95% +0.00001 to +0.0004). Buildings scale k: 0.851; 0.729 without the top row; 0.589 without the top 5.
recommendation: Keep the scored target uncapped, as the leaderboard is. For every variation, also report the paired gain with the top 10 A2024 rows removed and with a 50k cap. Treat a gain under about 0.004 that does not survive both as noise.

finding: Nearly half of the pooled D2 comes from separating the three lines' levels, because the null uses a single rate across all lines. Within-line ranking accounts for about 0.063 of C0's 0.120.
evidence: A predictor that knows only the line (exposure x line rate, level-matched) scores pooled 0.05694, which is 47% of C0's 0.12012. Its within-line D2 is 0.0000-0.0012.
recommendation: Judge ranking variations against the within-line part. The line levels are already captured by level matching.

field: C0 score dependence on large claims within 2023 (for cross-validation)
finding: The 2023 score is also driven by a few buildings fire rows, so customer-grouped cross-validation within 2023 will be dominated by whichever folds receive them.
evidence: fit2023 C0 pooled level-matched D2 0.11488 (bootstrap sd 0.0099). The top 5 rows, all buildings, carry 15.6% of the gain; dropping them gives -0.0110 (buildings 0.069 to 0.047). Capping at 50k gives -0.0091.
recommendation: Tune on a capped target, or stratify cross-validation folds so the rows over 50k are spread across them. Report the variance of the cross-validated deviance across folds.

field: search count and use of A2024 outcomes
finding: No model configuration was fitted or tuned. C0 was evaluated on A2024 only as a diagnostic, and no evaluation chose a model or a treatment. The capping recommendations rest on 2023 and developed evidence.
evidence: A2024 evaluations: 1 baseline (C0, reproduces 0.12012), 19 deterministic perturbations of the target or C0 (13 in s3, 6 in s6), and 200 random-row reference draws, 220 in all. A2024 outcomes were also used descriptively in s2 (large-claim counts, development factors). Scripts and logs: <a31 scratch>/data/d4_target_exposure/s1_target_exposure.py through s6_extra.py, with s1.log-s6.log. These contain aggregates only; holdout_B was not read.
recommendation: Count these 220 as diagnostics, not candidate configurations, when correcting for the search.
